caption:
Meta just gave its Muse AI agent a voice and a face.
Everyone in the US can now call or video chat with an animated Muse avatar on mobile, web and Mac.
You can interrupt it, pick from hundreds of voices, and it keeps working on tasks while you talk.

Would you video chat with an AI avatar?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Meta, TechCrunch
threads_text: Meta's Muse now takes voice and video calls in the US, with an animated avatar that reacts while you talk and keeps doing tasks in the background. Talking to an AI face is about to get very normal. Would you video chat with an AI avatar?

site_article.headline: Meta rolls out voice calls and animated avatars for Muse in the US
site_article.dek: Users of the Muse app on mobile, web and Mac can now talk to Meta's AI agent in real time and see an avatar that reacts as they speak.
site_article.summary: Meta said on November 5, 2026 that real-time voice conversations and expressive avatars are rolling out in its Muse app in the United States. The features, first previewed at Connect 2026, work on mobile, web and Mac, with AI Glasses and the Muse Charm device to follow.
site_article.seo_title: Meta Muse adds real-time voice and video avatar chats in the US
site_article.seo_description: Meta's Muse app now offers real-time voice and animated avatar conversations in the US on mobile, web and Mac, with glasses and Muse Charm next.
site_article.answer_summary: Muse users in the United States can now hold real-time voice conversations with Meta's AI agent and choose to see an animated avatar that reacts while they talk. It works on mobile, web and Mac.
site_article.hero_alt: Promotional image from Meta announcing voice and expressive avatars in the Muse app.

paragraphs.text: Meta began rolling out real-time voice conversations and expressive avatars in its Muse app in the United States on November 5, 2026, according to a post on the company's newsroom. The features are available on mobile, web and Mac. TechCrunch reported that Muse Voice is available to everyone in the U.S. and lets users call and video chat with Muse, the consumer AI agent Meta introduced earlier this fall.

Meta first previewed the voice and avatar features at its Connect 2026 conference in September. Unite.AI noted that the earlier event showed the concepts, while this announcement marks the actual rollout to users.

To start a conversation, users tap the phone icon in the top right corner of the Muse app, Meta said. Responses arrive in real time, and users can interrupt Muse while it is speaking. Meta said the agent can keep working on tasks in the background during a call, so a person can give instructions while walking or while their hands are busy.

Meta suggested several uses for the feature, including brainstorming, planning a trip, rehearsing for a job interview and running through a presentation or pitch. The company described voice as a way to think out loud with the assistant.

The avatar uses subtle expressions and gestures that match the tone of the conversation and reacts while the user is speaking, according to Meta. Users can choose to keep the conversation voice only, show the avatar alongside it, or switch to a full screen view. TechCrunch reported that the avatar, nicknamed Jolly, can be customized to look like a person, an animal or another character.
Meta said hundreds of voices and styles are available and can be changed at any time. Its examples include an energetic New Yorker style and a pirate style.
Meta announced the rollout in a blog post and on X through its chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, TechCrunch reported. Wang shared a demo featuring his own Muse avatar, a fluffy white dog.

The features run on two new models that Meta calls Muse Realtime Voice and Muse Realtime Avatar. According to Unite.AI, which summarized Meta's research write-up, the two form a single streaming system in which the avatar model follows the same stream as the voice model to keep speech, lip motion and expression in sync.

Unite.AI reported that Meta cut the work needed to generate each chunk of avatar video by a factor of 60 through distillation, and that the system produces portrait video at 25 frames per second with about 870 milliseconds between the end of a user's turn and the start of the reply. Generated avatar video carries an invisible Meta Video Seal watermark, the report said.

Meta said voice conversations are coming soon to its AI Glasses and to Muse Charm, without giving dates. TechCrunch reported that Meta plans to release Muse Charm, a small wearable with a screen that shows the avatar, before the end of 2026.

The update moves Muse closer to how people talk to each other rather than how they type into a search box. TechCrunch noted that Meta believes a more human looking agent could make people feel more connected to it. That same design choice is likely to draw attention from critics who worry about people forming attachments to AI characters.
The next test is whether Meta brings these voice and avatar chats to its AI Glasses and the Muse Charm wearable on schedule, and whether the rollout expands beyond the United States.
